description:
FOUND s470bx (Opus, resume) while probing #1237, PRE-EXISTING at fcf076f1 and
independent of it.  A `<...>` GLOB whose interpolation yields THREE OR MORE
pieces emits an N-ARY call to the BINARY `p-.`, and the whole program dies at
LOAD.

REPRO (scratch/s470bx/pglob3.pl), perl 5.40.3 vs PCL:

    my $h = "passwd";
    my @a = <a${h}b>;    # perl 1   PCL dies
    my @b = </etc/${h}>; # perl 1   PCL 1     (TWO pieces -- fine)
    my @c = </etc/$h*>;  # perl 2   PCL dies  (an ordinary spelling)

Emission (`./pl2cl`):

    (p-array-= @a (p-list-ctx (p-glob (p-. "a" $h "b"))))      ; 3 args
    (p-array-= @b (p-list-ctx (p-glob (p-. "/etc/" $h))))      ; 2 args, OK
    (p-array-= @c (p-list-ctx (p-glob (p-. "/etc/" $h "*"))))  ; 3 args

`cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:4366` is `(defun p-. (a b) ...)` -- BINARY.  The failure
is therefore not a wrong value but a dead file:

    Unhandled sb-int:simple-program-error: invalid number of arguments: 3
    0: (P-. "a" "passwd" "*") [external]

i.e. the #138 family's louder cousin: nothing is dropped, but the emitted form
cannot be called and the program never starts.  It reproduces on a `git
archive fcf076f1` extraction, so it is not #1043/#1231/#1237.

WHERE: whoever builds the `p-glob` argument from the angle-bracket contents
concatenates the interpolation pieces with a fold that assumes `p-.` is
n-ary.  Every other interpolation site in the compiler goes through
`p-string-concat` (n-ary, and overload-aware since #402/#119) -- rule 11 says
this site should reach the SAME helper rather than grow an arity fix of its
own.  Note the two-piece case works, which is why the bug survived: the common
`<$dir/*>` spelling is exactly two.

SIZE: an emission change (generation bump + the three artifacts + corpus-diff
+ emission-ab), so it is not a filler inside a runtime-only session.

RELATED: #488 (brace expansion is missing, so `glob("{$h}")` answers 0 where
perl answers 1) is a DIFFERENT gap in the same construct and stays open; the
`<{$h}>` spelling hits BOTH.

=== s543q (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-28, CODE 6a1301ed) -- ROSETTA: 0445-FASTA-format ===
The Rosetta census B found this shape in 0445-FASTA-format (LOUD): `while ( < $text > ) { ... }` -- a SPACED diamond around one variable, i.e. glob(" $text "), which perl splits on whitespace into the words of the string (no wildcard, so each word is returned as it is).  The pattern is built from THREE pieces (" ", $text, " ") and the emission's binary `p-.` gets three arguments: the program dies at the first iteration with a raw condition.
Neutral reproducer, run on the tree:
    my $s = "p q r";
    my @w = < $s >;
    print "@w\n";
    perl: p q r
    PCL : Unhandled sb-int:simple-program-error ... invalid number of arguments: 3   + a Lisp backtrace (exit 1)
    (the `while (my $x = < $s >)` iterator form the same; perl: [p][q][r])
CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (taken): 0445 with the loop over `glob(" $text ")` collected first (`my @gw = glob(" $text "); while (defined($_ = shift @gw))`) is byte-identical to perl -- this task is its only cause.  The raw condition is the UNTIDY half (#1427's census of internal errors that reach the user).
frequency: ordinary (Rosetta: 0445).


=== DONE (s543w, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-28; base 749eaf0e; generation v2-16900) ===
PCL's lowering, not PPI (rule 11, docs/interp-scan.md): the glob node took the interpolated pattern's string_concat node
APART (`add_child_flattening`) and `ExprToCL::gen_glob_form` joined the pieces with the binary `p-.`.  Now the
string_concat node is the glob's ONE child, lowered by the string lowering as any "..." is (`(p-glob (p-string-concat ...))`,
n-ary and overload-aware), the same shape the imported-`glob` override path already used; gen_glob_form's N-part arm is
unreachable and DIES naming the count (rule 12) instead of emitting an N-ary p-..
Probe table (14 rows, perl = tree): `<$d/*.$e>`, `<$a$b$c>`, `<${d}/$n.$e>`, `<@dirs>` (base printed ARRAY(0x1): the
array piece is joined with spaces now, several patterns), `<$h{k}/*>`, `<$fh>` (a readline: control), `glob("$a$b$c")`
(control), `< $s >` (0445's shape) and its `while (my $x = < $s >)` iterator, `<g-${h}.t>`, `<$d/*>`, `<$p>`,
`<${p}.t>`; `<$o->{dir}/*>` is a syntax error in perl and a drop in PCL (principle 9).
GUARD: Pl/t/readline-ternary-01.t "#1292: <$a$b$c>, <g-${h}.t>, < $s > and <@list> glob the interpolated string" (fails on
main).  PROGRAM: 0445 same.  #488 (brace expansion) is untouched.
